evidence.title: Collages (novel)
evidence.text: Collages, published in 1964, was Anaïs Nin's last published novel (excluding her erotica).

evidence.title: Collages (novel)
evidence.text: It is very different from the previous novels of the "Cities of the Interior" series, because it contains none of the familiar characters in those novels.

evidence.title: Collages (novel)
evidence.text: It is also different in that it takes place on two continents, has about two dozen important characters, and for the first time in Anaïs Nin's work the female lead is not seeking psychological wholeness.

evidence.title: Collages (novel)
evidence.text: Most of Anaïs Nin's other novels only have a few main characters, there is rarely much geographical movement in the other novels, and usually the lead character is a woman seeking psychological wholeness.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin: A Biography
evidence.text: Anaïs Nin: A Biography is Deirdre Bair's award-winning biography of writer Anaïs Nin.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin: A Biography
evidence.text: It is considered arguably by many to be the most comprehensive, well-researched, and scholarly biography available of Nin.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin: A Biography
evidence.text: Though the biography has received praise, it has also angered some fans of Anaïs Nin as well as some of her former associates, some of whom claim that Bair's critical and rigorous investigation of Anaïs Nin's life is unsympathetic.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin
evidence.text: Anaïs Nin (] ; born Angela Anaïs Juana Antolina Rosa Edelmira Nin y Culmell; February 21, 1903 – January 14, 1977) was an essayist and memoirist born to Cuban parents in France, where she was also raised.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin
evidence.text: She spent some time in Spain and Cuba, but lived most of her life in the United States, where she became an established author.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin
evidence.text: She wrote journals (which span more than 60 years, beginning when she was 11 years old and ending shortly before her death), novels, critical studies, essays, short stories, and erotica.

evidence.title: Anaïs Nin
evidence.text: A great deal of her work, including "Delta of Venus" and "Little Birds", was published posthumously.

evidence.title: Seduction of the Minotaur
evidence.text: Seduction of the Minotaur is an autobiographical novel by the mixed nationality writer Anaïs Nin, the last part of her "Cities of the Interior" sequence.

evidence.title: Seduction of the Minotaur
evidence.text: It is about a woman named Lillian, and her self-psychoanalysis.

evidence.title: Seduction of the Minotaur
evidence.text: The setting is taken from Anaïs' diary account of her first trip to Acapulco in 1947, and the novel repeats much of the first part of "The Diary of Anaïs Nin" volume V.

evidence.title: Seduction of the Minotaur
evidence.text: Since the author was concerned with psychology rather than physical adventure, there is actually less violence in the novel than in the diary account.

evidence.title: Seduction of the Minotaur
evidence.text: The exception is that the doctor allows himself to be shot because he is loved only as a doctor and never as a man, perhaps patterned after her understanding of Otto Rank's death.

evidence.title: Henry and June

evidence.title: Nearer the Moon
evidence.text: Nearer the Moon: From a Journal of Love (full title "Nearer the Moon: From a Journal of Love, the Unexpurgated Diary of Anaïs Nin (1937–1939)") is a 1996 book based upon material excerpted from the unpublished diaries of Anaïs Nin.

evidence.title: Nearer the Moon
evidence.text: It corresponds temporally to part of Nin's published diaries.

evidence.title: Nearer the Moon
evidence.text: It consists mainly of material that was left out of the published version because it would have hurt people involved or their relationships with Anaïs Nin had it been published at the time.
